title: Total IgE
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows the total level of antibodies linked to allergies.
why: For a possible allergy, asthma, atopic dermatitis (eczema), and sometimes for possible worms.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you take steroids or allergy medicines
If your allergy is flaring up now
If you were recently treated for worms

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting, 4 to 8 hours without food. Water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No alcohol, fatty food, or hard workouts.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow, and the skin is wiped
Blood is drawn into a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days
This test does not show what exactly you are allergic to. There are separate tests for that

faq.q: If IgE is normal, does that mean no allergy?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It can be normal even with an allergy. Your doctor looks at it together with your symptoms.

faq.q: Why is my child's IgE high?
faq.a: There are many reasons: allergy, worms, or eczema. Your doctor will find out which.

reminders.text: IgE blood test tomorrow. It is usually done fasting. Water is fine.
